title: DC-area forecast: A few lingering showers or a storm tonight; then much-improved holiday weather
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Late afternoon and early evening temperatures near 80 with some clouds around and slowly improving humidity. A few brief rains linger tonight, but the bulk should focus west and south of the Beltway.

What's next? Lower humidity tomorrow holds through Labor Day. Mainly bright skies and pleasant temperatures both days. Warming up again Tuesday and Wednesday, with highs near 90 by Thursday.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: A few lingering showers or a storm taper off tonight. Heaviest and most widespread activity stays west and south of the Beltway. Slowly drier air filtering in (dew points dipping through the 60s) and fewer clouds overnight. Lows near 60 to mid-60s. Confidence: Medium

Tomorrow (Sunday): Mainly sunny and less humid, with highs near 80 to mid-80s. Light to moderate breezes from the northeast. A few afternoon clouds and a pop-up sprinkle or shower are slightly possible but we’re optimistic it’s a solid outdoor activity day. Confidence: Medium-High 😎 Nice Day!

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow night: Partly cloudy and comfortable, with lows again near 60 to mid-60s. A lighter breeze from the northeast. A patch or two of fog is possible. Confidence: Medium-High

❤️ How to support Capital Weather

Help sustain an independent Capital Weather by becoming a free or paid supporter. Learn more at capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

A pleasant Labor Day is expected with mostly clear to partly cloudy skies, highs again in the upper 70s to low 80s, and comfortable humidity (dew points mainly in the upper 50s to low 60s). It should be a great day to enjoy the extra day off and get outside! Confidence: Medium

The pleasant stretch continues Tuesday, with relatively low humidity and highs in the low to mid-80s under partly to mostly sunny skies. Temperatures trend up Wednesday, with highs potentially eyeing 90, while humidity begins to creep back in. A shower chance could also return Wednesday evening. Confidence: Medium

By Thursday, highs again reach for 90 as humidity continues to build, with dew points rising into the upper 60s and low 70s. We’ll have to see if a shower or storm chance enters the picture. Confidence: Medium

Today’s daily digit — 6/10: The muggiest and cloudiest day of the long weekend, but brighter skies and drier air are on the doorstep. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

DC weather history for September 5

Torrential rains tied to the 1935 Labor Day Hurricane produced record rainfall and widespread flooding, while in 1979 Tropical Storm David brought wind damage, flooding, and even tornadoes to the region.
